# `prefer-sentinel-termination`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports manual allocation of an extra element followed by writing a zero
terminator.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`allocSentinel` and `dupeSentinel` encode the sentinel in the type and keep
allocation size and termination coupled.

## When it fires

It applies to recognized simple buffer construction patterns with an unambiguous
zero terminator: after the allocation the buffer is only indexed, sliced,
reached through `.ptr`, or freed. A buffer that is stored, returned, passed
whole, or measured with `.len` counts the zero as an element, and
`allocSentinel` would shorten it by one.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn dupeZ(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, src: []const u8) ![:0]u8 {
    const buf = try allocator.alloc(u8, src.len + 1);
    @memcpy(buf[0..src.len], src);
    buf[src.len] = 0;
    return buf[0..src.len :0];
}
```
